messages:
Aisha Bello: Dropping the latest MTTR baseline + a proposal for “time-to-suspect-change” (TTSC) so we can start weekly reporting without bikeshedding every time.

Baseline sheet (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/RI-SRE/mttr-baseline (tab: “2025W06 baseline”) 
MTTR dashboard (Grafana): https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/sre-mttr/incident-mttr-baseline?orgId=1
Draft TTSC dashboard (WIP): https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/sre-ttsc/time-to-suspect-change?orgId=1

Open questions:
1) MTTR start/end: do we stick to “page fired” -> “incident mitigated” as recorded in incident timeline? 
2) TTSC: definition I’m using = time from incident declared -> first *documented* suspected cause category (deploy/config/saturation/unknown). But what’s “documented” in practice (Slack, incident timeline, bot signal?)
3) cadence: propose we publish weekly every Mon 10am PT in #eng-sre + email Neha + SRE leads.

Would love quick ✅ / edits today so I can lock this for Phase 0 metrics.

Sean Gallagher: Thanks Aisha. On (1) I’m +1 to page->mitigated, but only if we’re consistent about what “mitigated” means. Some incidents get “stable-ish” then linger 2h while we backfill capacity.

Rafael Mendes: ^ yeah. We’ve been inconsistent: some ICs mark “mitigation” when 5xx drops, others when latency returns to SLO. If we don’t normalize we’ll just measure our own behavior.

Aisha Bello: Agree. In the sheet I used the incident timeline fields from incident tool (the “Mitigated” timestamp), but I can add a second metric: page->SLO recovered (based on the primary SLO burn alert clearing). That gives us a more objective line.

Miles Thornton: Please do. Multi-region incidents especially: us-east “mitigated” might mean we failed traffic to us-west but the customer impact continues depending on routing.

Logan Wright: On (2) TTSC: I strongly prefer using something machine-capturable. Slack freeform is going to be messy.

Allison Grant: +1. If you want TTSC to be a leading indicator of “bot usefulness”, we need a concrete event. Otherwise we’ll argue forever about whether “maybe deploy?” counts.

Sean Gallagher: What if we define “suspect change identified” as the first time someone posts either:
- a deploy link / release event and says “likely related”, or
- a config diff link and says “likely related”, or
- saturation dashboard link + says “we’re saturated”

But that’s still text parsing.

Jacob Stein: We can instrument this pretty cleanly if we add a lightweight action to the incident bot. E.g. responder clicks a Slack message button: “Mark as suspected cause” with dropdown (deploy/config/saturation/other). That emits an event we can chart.

Aisha Bello: That would be ideal long-term. For Phase 0 I’m trying to baseline using existing artifacts so we don’t block on bot work.

Talia Benson: If we need something now, could we use a process rule: IC (or scribe) must add “Suspected cause:” line in the incident doc within 30 min? Then TTSC is incident declared -> that timestamp.

Rafael Mendes: The problem is adoption. Half the time the scribe is also firefighting.

Neha Kapoor: Jumping in. Two things:
- I don’t want TTSC to become a “gotcha” metric. It should be directional + improve with tooling.
- We *do* need a consistent weekly view to track the program.

If Phase 0 TTSC is manually-tagged for a subset of Sev0/Sev1 incidents, that’s ok, but please make the definition explicit.

Aisha Bello: 👍 makes sense. Proposal for Phase 0:
- Scope TTSC measurement to Sev0/Sev1 only (lower volume, more consistent postmortems)
- TTSC source of truth = first timestamp when IC/scribe adds a “Suspected change:” entry in the incident timeline (same place we track “Customer comms sent”, etc.)
- If no suspected change identified, leave null (don’t default to end-of-incident)

Then when the bot adds the “suspected change heuristic”, we compare bot timestamp vs human timestamp.

Sean Gallagher: That works. But we need to ensure timeline has a standard field, not random text. Right now it’s freeform entries.

Jacob Stein: I can add a quick template snippet to the incident tool runbook today:
“Suspected change: <deploy|config|capacity/saturation|unknown> – link(s)”

And the bot can remind in-thread after 10m if empty (non-paging reminder, just a nudge).

Rafael Mendes: Reminder is good but please don’t spam #incidents threads. Maybe only in eng-sre channel threads or only if the channel is allowlisted.

Aisha Bello: Yeah, no new spam. For now, just a runbook update + we’ll ask rotations to follow it for 2 weeks.

Allison Grant: For “page->SLO recovered”: which SLO are we using? We have per-route and per-model SLOs. A lot of incidents are localized.

Aisha Bello: For baseline: primary customer-visible SLO for the impacted product surface (chat/generate/embeddings), chosen from the incident metadata. If missing, we use the global “API availability” SLO as fallback. I’ll add that logic to the dashboard description.

Miles Thornton: And for multi-region, can we tag whether the incident was single region vs multi? TTSC is harder when it’s a partial failover.

Aisha Bello: Yes. Sheet already has “region_scope” column (single/multi/global). Dashboard has a filter but it’s currently broken for a couple incidents (missing labels). I’ll fix.

Logan Wright: Re dashboards: can you add annotation markers for deploy/config events? That’ll help sanity-check TTSC.

Aisha Bello: On it. There’s a draft overlay panel here (currently only us-east): https://grafana.redwoodinference.com/d/sre-change-overlay/change-annotations-overlay?orgId=1

Sean Gallagher: Cadence (3): Mon 10am PT works. Can we include:
- weekly median MTTR (Sev0/1)
- P75 MTTR
- median TTSC
- count of incidents with TTSC captured (coverage)

And a short “top drivers” note (deploy/config/saturation/unknown).

Talia Benson: I can own the recurring calendar + template post. We should keep the narrative small: 5 bullets max.

Neha Kapoor: Great. Also include one “callout” each week: either a win (bot helped) or a gap (missing signal). That makes it actionable.

Rafael Mendes: One more nuance: when we say “incident declared”, do we mean first #incidents post or when we flip to Sev1 in the incident tool?

Aisha Bello: I used incident tool “Declared” timestamp. It’s more consistent than Slack. If the incident starts in Slack and is declared 15m later, TTSC will look better than reality though.

Sean Gallagher: That’s fine for now as long as we’re consistent. Later we can measure “alert fired -> declared” separately (that’s another pain area).

Jacob Stein: Action items I’m hearing:
- Aisha: add page->SLO recovered metric + fix region_scope filter + document definitions in dashboard
- Jacob: add runbook template line for “Suspected change” + ask rotations to use for 2 weeks
- Talia: set up weekly post cadence + template

Did I miss anything?

Aisha Bello: That’s it. I’ll update the sheet + dashboard descriptions today and drop a short “definition v0” note in Confluence (or just pin in #eng-sre). Thanks all.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: 

Neha Kapoor: :+1: Please CC me on the first weekly post so I can make sure it matches reliability program reporting.

Rafael Mendes: :white_check_mark: I’ll message the on-call leads to start capturing “Suspected change” in timeline starting next rotation.
